thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: [P1] Cross-region routing flap detected — increased 5xx and 404 spikes for us-west1 => eu-west2 traffic, latency elevated. Auto-mitigation did not engage. See runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cross-region-routing|cross-region-routing>

maya: Ack. I'm oncall. Observing ~35% 502/504 and a rising 404 tail for certain clients. @aj can you pull up routing diffs from the last promotion?

aj: Looking now. There's a recent promotion at 03:06 UTC that replaced a set of route-variants. The control-plane shows the new policy, but a subset of edge nodes still advertise the old A records due to stale DNS cache entries (edge TTLs were extended during a previous maintenance). The result: some edges are sending to legacy backends that were removed -> 404s.

tom: That matches traces — client IPs hitting eu-west2 are sometimes routed to an internal hostname that no longer resolves on the backend farm. We also see an uptick in TCP retransmits between edges and origin.

lena: Quick mitigation options: 1) force a control-plane cache flush on all edge nodes; 2) temporarily reintroduce compatibility listener on origin to accept legacy hostnames (short-term); 3) shorten edge DNS TTLs and purge caches. Option 1+3 fastest. Thoughts?

ops_lead: Approve cache flush + DNS TTL adjustment. No origin changes yet; avoid extra deploys if possible. Keep changes reversible. Notify CS.

aj: Executing edge cache flush and DNS TTL reset now:
```
# flush edge control-plane caches
rwctl edge flush --scope eu-west2 --keys "route:*" --reason "incident: stale edge cache"

# set DNS TTL lower for steering records
rwctl dns update --zone redwood-steer --record steering.eu-west2 --ttl 30
```

incident-bot: Automated: cache flush initiated by aj at 3512345890. DNS TTL update pushed. Monitoring propagation.

natalie-cs: CS: initial reports — 5 tenants with intermittent failures, one big customer reports checkout failures. We've opened high-priority notes and asked for ETA before we send customer update.

maya: Noted. @natalie-cs gather tenant IDs and whether they're currently impacted. I'll prioritize a temporary pin/override to make sure in-flight sessions complete.

tom: Putting an immediate region-preference override for us-west1 callers who resolved to eu-west2 so they fall back to origin region for 20m:
```
rwctl routing override --match "client_region:us-west1 and target_region:eu-west2" --preference origin --duration 20m --reason "incident safety pin"
```

netops-bot: Observability: error-rate across affected edges dropping from 35% -> 9% within 6 minutes after cache flush + TTL change. 95p latency reduced 2.4s -> 380ms. Continuing to monitor.

lena: Running synthetic checkout tests against the affected path — canaries show success after override. Recommend keeping DNS TTL low for 1 hour and then raise gradually while observing.

sre-manager: Preparing incident bridge and timeline. Please collect policy diffs and edge cache logs and store artifacts in /incidents/3512345678/artifacts. Assigning postmortem to eng-platform and netops.

maya: Bridge up: meet.google.com/incident-3512. I've uploaded the cache flush logs and DNS diffs.

aj: Root cause hypothesis: during the promotion we swapped route variants but did not invalidate (or we extended) edge DNS/route TTLs in a prior ops window. The promotion assumed immediate convergence; edges with long TTL hit removed backends. Short-term fix: ensure promotions include a targeted cache invalidation and TTL alignment step.

ops_lead: Action items immediately: 1) keep override for 20m, 2) keep DNS TTL at 30s for 60m, 3) run full flush across all regions once stable. Post-incident: add pre-promotion check for edge TTLs and add a gating step in the promotion pipeline.

natalie-cs: Sent customer update — high level note + ETA. CS will follow up with impacted customers with timeline and compensation if needed.

lena: I'll open a PR to add a pre-promote CI check that fails if any edge-config TTL > 5m for steering records and add an automated cache flush step post-promotion. Drafting now.

tom: Removing the override in 18m if metrics hold. Will keep canary at 5% traffic for 30m post-change.

incident-bot: STATUS: recovering. Error rate 6% (was 35%). Mitigations: edge cache flush, DNS TTL decrease, routing override, canary validation. Monitoring for 45m.

maya: Handoff: I'm stepping out for a short break. @tom take lead, @sre-manager you're on escalation. I'll review the RCA draft when I'm back.

tom: Taking lead. Will run full regional flush after 10m and coordinate with netops for a staged TTL increase.

sre-manager: Please add timeline and artifact links to the incident ticket and schedule RCA meeting within 48h. Also include customer impact summary from CS.

incident-bot: INCIDENT PROVISIONALLY RESOLVED: routing and errors back to baseline after mitigations. Incident remains open until RCA complete. Thanks to responders.
